decisions.reason: Interior local integrability does not ensure finite signed entropy integrals for tests reaching t=0. For example U(t,x)=1/t with F=0, eta(z)=z^2 and q=0 has locally integrable compositions on every interior compact set but eta(U)=t^-2 is not integrable on (0,tau) times a spatial compact set of positive measure. The initial entropy clause omitted the corresponding test-support qualification. Added explicit absolute integrability of eta(U) and all q_j(U) on every such boundary slab and specified all nonnegative initial-boundary tests; the sign, compatibility and initial term are preserved.

The Definition supplies the equation, C1 flux, Jacobian, ordered distinct real eigenvalues, Rankine-Hugoniot equality and all Lax inequalities explicitly. These are well-defined on any open state domain: they use only flux values and derivatives at the stated states, with no convex combination or entropy pair. The earlier conservation-system item works on convex domains but its convex-entropy construction is not invoked here. Dafermos section 8.3 equation (8.3.1) was consulted for the characteristic inequalities; his general chapter 7 setting additionally assumes convexity and C3 flux, which are not necessary for this locally explicit definition. Narrowing this sound definition would discard scope without repairing a mathematical defect.

The exact statement says let I subset R and Omega subset R^d be open, so both sets are open and Q is open. The trace supplier also requires I merely open. All regular-distribution operations used in F3 apply on any open set Q, as explicitly stated in the conservation definition and its regular-distribution supplier; connectedness of I is not used. Under Countable Choice the spacetime normal (-s,n) is nonzero, hence Sigma is null; measurable finite changes there preserve local integrability and every regular pairing, while identical open-side fields have identical C1 traces. No time-boundary assertion is made.
